claims.text: A high density of nanoscale, thermally stable precipitates concentrated at grain boundaries governs high-temperature plastic strain in fusion plasma-facing structural alloys.
A high density of nanoscale, thermally stable precipitates concentrated at grain boundaries governs high-temperature toughness in fusion plasma-facing structural alloys.
Grain-boundary precipitates locally pin dislocation motion.
Grain-boundary precipitates delay dynamic recrystallization.
A targeted heat treatment can refine and increase the density of nanoscale grain-boundary precipitates without changing the overall alloy composition.
Refined precipitates inhibit dislocation motion by acting as pinning points.
Precipitate-mediated inhibition of dislocation motion suppresses dynamic recovery.
Precipitate-mediated inhibition of dislocation motion suppresses dynamic recrystallization.
Suppression of recovery and recrystallization limits the ease of plastic deformation.
The precipitate-stabilized microstructure adjusts strain-hardening behavior under high-temperature stress.
A more stable precipitate-containing microstructure enhances toughness under high-temperature stress.
The tailored heat-treated material will have greater high-temperature toughness than the same alloy with a conventional precipitate distribution.
The tailored heat-treated material will show measurably different high-temperature plastic-strain behavior from the baseline.
The altered plastic-strain behavior may include a higher yield point.
The altered plastic-strain behavior may include delayed onset of rapid plastic flow.
The hypothesis is expected to hold for similarly composed and similarly processed materials at temperatures up to approximately 1200°C under loads typical of fusion plasma-facing components.
The hypothesis may not apply to alloys with vastly different compositions.
Extreme irradiation can alter precipitate stability and thereby place the material outside the proposed regime.
Irradiation effects and variations in precipitate stability may affect the magnitude of toughness and plastic-strain enhancement.
Failure to obtain both a statistically significant toughness improvement and a measurable change in dislocation or dynamic-recrystallization behavior would falsify the proposed mechanism.
